resources.string: This phone has no step counter
Passo counts steps only with the phone’s own step counter sensor, and this device doesn’t have one. There is nothing Passo can count here.
Every step, even with the app closed.
With your phone’s own step counter, in the background, and again by itself after a restart.
No account and no internet permission: Passo keeps your steps on the phone and sends them nowhere.
It is light on the battery
The counting is done by a low-power chip; Passo wakes the phone only when there is a reason to.
Height and weight are used only for distance and calories. Skip them and average values are used; you can change them any time in Settings.
Sex, for the step length estimate
Around 8,000 steps a day the health benefits start to level off: a 2022 study of 15 cohorts found most of the gain below that, and less and less above it.
Lets Passo read the phone’s step counter. Without it nothing can be counted.
Android shows a fixed notification while an app counts in the background; with notifications allowed it carries today’s steps. Turned down, counting goes on all the same.
Turned down. Passo cannot count without it: you can allow it now or later, from Today.

Some phones stop apps in the background to save battery, and Passo would stop counting with them. If counting ever stops, let Passo run in the background: on most phones it is the app’s Battery page, “Unrestricted”.
